propositions.name: quantity_of_matter_definition
propositions.statement: The quantity of matter of a body is fixed by the product of its density and its bulk.
propositions.quote: The quantity of matter is the measure of the same, arising from its density and bulk conjunctly.

propositions.name: mass_proportional_to_weight
propositions.statement: The quantity of matter of a body is proportional to its weight.
propositions.quote: for it is proportional to the weight, as I have found by experiments on pendulums, very accurately made, which shall be shewn hereafter.

propositions.name: quantity_of_motion_definition
propositions.statement: The quantity of motion of a body is fixed by the product of its velocity and its quantity of matter.
propositions.quote: The quantity of motion is the measure of the same, arising from the velocity and quantity of matter conjunctly.

propositions.name: motion_of_whole_sums_parts
propositions.statement: The motion of a whole body equals the arithmetic sum of the motions of its parts.
propositions.quote: The motion of the whole is the sum of the motions of all the parts; and therefore in a body double in quantity, with equal velocity, the motion is double

propositions.name: vis_insita_persists_state
propositions.statement: Every body has an innate power of resisting by which it endeavours to persevere in its present state of rest or uniform right-line motion.
propositions.quote: The vis insita, or innate force of matter, is a power of resisting, by which every body, as much as in it lies, endeavours to persevere in its present state

propositions.name: impressed_force_changes_state
propositions.statement: An impressed force is an action exerted upon a body to change its state of rest or uniform right-line motion.
propositions.quote: An impressed force is an action exerted upon a body, in order to change its state, either of rest, or of moving uniformly forward in a right line.

propositions.name: centripetal_force_toward_centre
propositions.statement: A centripetal force is one by which bodies are drawn or tend toward a point as a centre.
propositions.quote: A centripetal force is that by which bodies are drawn or impelled, or any way tend, towards a point as to a centre.

propositions.name: accelerative_force_generates_velocity
propositions.statement: The accelerative quantity of a centripetal force is proportional to the velocity it generates in a given time.
propositions.quote: The accelerative quantity of a centripetal force is the measure of the same, proportional to the velocity which it generates in a given time.

propositions.name: weight_measured_by_counter_force
propositions.statement: The weight of a body is known by the equal and contrary force just sufficient to hinder its descent.
propositions.quote: it is always known by the quantity of an equal and contrary force just sufficient to hinder the descent of the body.

propositions.name: absolute_time_flows_equably
propositions.statement: Absolute time, of itself and from its own nature, flows equably without regard to anything external.
propositions.quote: Absolute, true, and mathematical time, of itself, and from its own nature flows equably without regard to anything external, and by another name is called duration

propositions.name: absolute_space_immovable
propositions.statement: Absolute space in its own nature remains always similar and immovable.
propositions.quote: Absolute space, in its own nature, without regard to anything external, remains always similar and immovable.

propositions.name: space_uniform_in_figure_and_magnitude
propositions.statement: Absolute and relative spaces are the same in figure and magnitude, so geometric relations do not depend on which space is meant.
propositions.quote: Absolute and relative space, are the same in figure and magnitude; but they do not remain always numerically the same.

propositions.name: no_perfectly_equable_motion_exists
propositions.statement: There may be no equable motion by which time can be accurately measured.
propositions.quote: It may be, that there is no such thing as an equable motion, whereby time may be accurately measured.

propositions.name: duration_independent_of_motion
propositions.statement: The duration of the existence of things remains the same whether motions are swift, slow, or none at all.
propositions.quote: The duration or perseverance of the existence of things remains the same, whether the motions are swift or slow, or none at all

propositions.name: natural_days_truly_unequal
propositions.statement: The natural days are truly unequal though commonly used as equal measures of time.
propositions.quote: For the natural days are truly unequal, though they are commonly considered as equal, and used for a measure of time

propositions.name: eclipses_and_pendulums_calibrate_time
propositions.statement: The correction from apparent to absolute time is evinced by pendulum clock experiments and by eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter.
propositions.quote: The necessity of which equation, for determining the times of a phenomenon, is evinced as well from the experiments of the pendulum clock, as by eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter

propositions.name: order_of_time_and_space_immutable
propositions.statement: The order of the parts of time and the order of the parts of space are immutable.
propositions.quote: As the order of the parts of time is immutable, so also is the order of the parts of space.

propositions.name: primary_places_are_immovable
propositions.statement: The primary places of things must be immovable, since it is absurd that they should be moveable.
propositions.quote: It is from their essence or nature that they are places; and that the primary places of things should be moveable, is absurd.

propositions.name: immovable_places_span_infinity
propositions.statement: The only immovable places are those which from infinity to infinity retain the same given position one to another.
propositions.quote: Now no other places are immovable but those that, from infinity to infinity, do all retain the same given position one to another

propositions.name: true_motion_requires_impressed_force
propositions.statement: True motion is neither generated nor altered except by some force impressed upon the body moved.
propositions.quote: True motion is neither generated nor altered, but by some force impressed upon the body moved

propositions.name: relative_motion_alters_without_force
propositions.statement: Relative motion may be generated or altered without any force impressed on the body itself, by acting on bodies to which it is compared.
propositions.quote: relative motion may be generated or altered without any force impressed upon the body. For it is sufficient only to impress some force on other bodies with which the former is compared

propositions.name: rectilinear_uniform_inertial_motion
propositions.statement: A body free of impressed force would move in a right line with a uniform motion.
propositions.quote: would not deviate towards the earth, but would go off from it in a right line, and that with an uniform motion, if the resistance of the air was taken away.

propositions.name: right_line_frame_invariant
propositions.statement: There is a definite fact of the matter about what counts as a right line for a body free of impressed force.
propositions.quote: were it not for the opposition of a contrary force which restrains them to, and detains them in their orbits, which I therefore call centripetal, would fly off in right lines, with an uniform motion.

propositions.name: velocities_add_arithmetically
propositions.statement: Velocities of a body, a vehicle carrying it, and the earth carrying the vehicle combine by simple arithmetic addition and subtraction.
propositions.quote: but a sailor walks in the ship towards the east, with 1 part of the said velocity; then the sailor will be moved truly in immovable space towards the east

propositions.name: simultaneous_velocities_across_bodies
propositions.statement: The velocities of the earth, the ship, and the sailor can all be evaluated at the same instant and combined into one true velocity in immovable space.
propositions.quote: the sailor will be moved truly in immovable space towards the east, with a velocity of 10001 parts, and relatively on the earth towards the west, with a velocity of 9 of those parts.

propositions.name: rest_is_mutual_among_truly_resting_bodies
propositions.statement: It is a property of rest that bodies really at rest are at rest in respect to one another.
propositions.quote: It is a property of rest, that bodies really at rest do rest in respect to one another.

propositions.name: surroundings_carry_included_bodies
propositions.statement: If a surrounding whole is moved, the bodies included within it partake of the motion, as a kernel moves with its shell.
propositions.quote: if the shell moves, the kernel will also move, as being part of the whole, without any removal from near the shell.

propositions.name: possible_body_absolutely_at_rest
propositions.statement: It is possible that in the remote regions of the fixed stars, or beyond them, some body is absolutely at rest.
propositions.quote: as it is possible, that in the remote regions of the fixed stars, or perhaps far beyond them, there may be some body absolutely at rest

propositions.name: axis_recession_effect_distinguishes_absolute
propositions.statement: The forces of receding from the axis of circular motion are the effects that distinguish absolute from relative motion.
propositions.quote: The effects which distinguish absolute from relative motion are, the forces of receding from the axis of circular motion.

propositions.name: true_circular_motion_produces_ascent
propositions.statement: The absolute circular motion of the water shows itself by the ascent of the water up the sides of the vessel.
propositions.quote: This ascent of the water shows its endeavour to recede from the axis of its motion; and the true and absolute circular motion of the water, which is here directly contrary to the relative, discovers itself

propositions.name: recession_independent_of_ambient_translation
propositions.statement: The endeavour of the water to recede from the axis does not depend on any translation of the water with respect to the ambient bodies.
propositions.quote: this endeavour does not depend upon any translation of the water in respect of the ambient bodies, nor can true circular motion be defined by such translation.

propositions.name: one_real_circular_motion_per_body
propositions.statement: Any one revolving body has only one real circular motion, with only one corresponding power of receding from its axis as its proper and adequate effect.
propositions.quote: There is only one real circular motion of any one revolving body, corresponding to only one power of endeavouring to recede from its axis of motion, as its proper and adequate effect

propositions.name: cord_tension_measures_true_rotation
propositions.statement: The tension of a cord connecting two revolving globes discovers the endeavour of the globes to recede from the axis and permits computation of their circular motions.
propositions.quote: we might, from the tension of the cord, discover the endeavour of the globes to recede from the axis of their motion, and from thence we might compute the quantity of their circular motions.

propositions.name: true_rotation_detectable_in_vacuum
propositions.statement: Both the quantity and the determination of a true circular motion can be found even in an immense vacuum with nothing external to compare against.
propositions.quote: And thus we might find both the quantity and the determination of this circular motion, even in an immense vacuum, where there was nothing external or sensible with which the globes could be compared.
